headline: Norway's surgical efficiency cuts through Senegal's possession blitz
story: Senegal arrived with a gameplan—aggressive pressing, ball dominance, suffocating Norway into errors. For 47 minutes, it worked. Then Norway's clinical edge took over. Two goals in five minutes after half-time, a third ten minutes later, and Norway had seized a 3-1 lead while Senegal's 51% possession and 7.8 high-press phases yielded nothing. The momentum reversed entirely in that spell. Senegal rallied with a late goal, but Norway had already translated scraps into gold.

The numbers reveal the gulf. Senegal created 2.05 xG from 16 shots—only four on target. Norway managed just 1.5 xG but buried three. Haaland's dominance (8.8 rating) was the difference: he terrorised a Senegal side that pressed frantically (36 forced turnovers) but left themselves exposed on the counter. Senegal's 4-2-3-1 midfield, designed for control and pressing, couldn't deal with Norway's devastating pace on the break. A missed big chance at 90+9' (xG 0.46) summed up their day—possession without precision.

keyMoment.text: Norway's third goal (xG 0.30) breaks the match open, Senegal's press strategy in tatters

home.verdict: Clinical opportunism and Haaland's lethality beat the press.
points: Haaland's 8.8 rating: the lethal focal point in transition, justifying the 4-3-3 width
Three goals from 1.5 xG: ruthless efficiency despite sitting deep (only 3.9 press phases)
Early second-half sequence: two goals in five minutes (48', 53', 58') broke Senegal's midfield rhythm permanently

away.verdict: Dominance crumbled because finishing didn't match ambition.
points: Only 4 on-target from 16 shots: wastefulness cost the match (2.05 xG, 2 goals)
90+9' miss (xG 0.46): last-gasp chance—conversion reverses the scoreline entirely
7.8 high-press phases exposed the defence on the counter; 51% possession wasted without ruthlessness

statLine: Senegal dominated with 51% possession and 16 shots; Norway won with 40% possession and three lethal finishes from 1.5 expected goals.
